questions.question: What was the targeted growth rate of the Second Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan of India targeted a growth rate of **4.5% (0.045)**.
 
• It was formulated based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, focusing on rapid industrialization.
 
• The plan covered the period from **1956 to 1961**.
 
• It emphasized the development of heavy industries, steel plants, and infrastructure to strengthen the industrial base of the economy.
 
• The actual achieved growth rate during the Second Plan period was approximately **4.27%**, slightly below the targeted rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Model**

 
 
• Developed by statistician **P.C. Mahalanobis**, this model emphasized the importance of the heavy industrial sector for long-term economic growth.
 
• It advocated for a higher allocation of resources to capital goods industries, such as steel, machinery, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• India adopted the Five-Year Plan system in **1951** to achieve planned economic development.
 
• The plans were inspired by the Soviet model of centralized economic planning.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture, while the Second Plan shifted focus to industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• Established in **1950**, the Planning Commission was responsible for formulating and monitoring Five-Year Plans.
 
• It was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in 2015 under the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
 
 
• **Heavy Industries**
 
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan led to the establishment of steel plants in Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur with the assistance of countries like the USSR, Germany, and the UK.
 
• It prioritized industries requiring high investment and long gestation periods for boosting overall economic growth.

questions.question: Whose name was recorded in the Guinness Book of World Records for recording 28 songs in one day in 1993?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumar Sanu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kumar Sanu**, a renowned playback singer in India, set the Guinness World Record in 1993 for recording 28 songs in a single day.
 
• He achieved this feat during the peak of his career, showcasing his incredible vocal stamina and versatility.
 
• Kumar Sanu is known for his melodious voice and has sung in multiple languages, making him a household name in the Indian music industry.
 
• The record highlights his dedication and contribution to Indian music, particularly in the Bollywood industry.
 
• He received the prestigious **Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer** for five consecutive years (1990-1994), further solidifying his legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Playback Singing:**

 
 
• Playback singing is a unique feature of Indian cinema where singers record songs in advance, and actors lip-sync to them during filming.
 
• It allows the industry to leverage specialized vocal talents like Kumar Sanu for songs used in films.
 
 
 
• **Guinness World Records:**
 
 
• Guinness World Records is a global organization that verifies and catalogs extraordinary achievements across various fields.
 
• Kumar Sanu’s record for recording 28 songs in one day is a testament to his exceptional talent and work ethic.
 
 
 
• **Bollywood Music Industry:**
 
 
• Bollywood is one of the largest film industries in the world, known for its musical films and extensive use of songs.
 
• Kumar Sanu has been a key contributor to Bollywood music during the 1990s, often collaborating with legendary composers like Nadeem-Shravan.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Kumar Sanu:**
 
 
• Born as Kedarnath Bhattacharya, Kumar Sanu is a Padma Shri awardee (2009) for his contribution to Indian music.
 
• He has sung over 20,000 songs in various Indian languages, making him one of the most prolific playback singers in history.

questions.question: Which of the following is a popular dance form of Punjab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhangra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhangra** is one of the most popular and lively dance forms originating from Punjab, India.
 
• It is performed during harvest festivals like **Baisakhi** and other celebratory occasions.
 
• The dance form incorporates traditional Punjabi music using instruments like the **dhol**, tumbi, chimta, and tabla.
 
• Bhangra involves energetic and rhythmic movements, often reflecting the vibrancy and enthusiasm of Punjabi culture.
 
• Over time, Bhangra has gained global recognition and is now performed at international events and competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghumar:** A traditional dance form of Rajasthan, performed by women in colorful attire during festivals and special occasions.
 
• **Chhau:** A semi-classical dance from eastern India (Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal), often depicting themes from mythology and performed with masks.
 
• **Garba:** A folk dance from Gujarat performed during Navratri, characterized by circular movements and clapping.
 
• **Punjabi Music:** The energetic beats of the **dhol** and tumbi used in Bhangra reflect the agricultural roots and celebratory spirit of Punjab.
 
• **Global Influence:** Bhangra is widely recognized worldwide, with its fusion into modern music genres like hip-hop and electronic dance music.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are mentioned in Articles _____ of the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 36-51**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Constitution of India, covering Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSPs aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life and are considered non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable.
 
• They are guidelines for the state to ensure socio-economic justice and establish a welfare state.
 
• These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and were included in the Indian Constitution to promote equitable development.
 
• Some important DPSPs include provisions for securing a uniform civil code, promoting cottage industries, ensuring equal pay for equal work, and protecting the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights vs. DPSP:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are non-justiciable and serve as moral obligations for the government.
 
• In case of conflict, courts strive to harmonize both; however, Fundamental Rights generally prevail.
 
 
 
• **Classification of DPSPs:**
 
 
• **Socialistic Principles:** Focus on social welfare, such as providing adequate means of livelihood and improving public health.
 
• **Gandhian Principles:** Reflect Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals, like promoting cottage industries and organizing village panchayats.
 
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles:** Encourage economic and legal reforms, international peace, and protection of monuments.
 
 
 
• **Significance of DPSPs:**
 
 
• They act as a framework for governance and policymaking, guiding the government toward socio-economic justice.
 
• Though not enforceable, they often influence the judiciary in interpreting laws and policies.
 
 
 
• **Amendments Related to DPSPs:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, added new DPSPs, like promoting equal justice and free legal aid, and safeguarding forests and wildlife.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, made education for children a fundamental right but retained promoting free and compulsory education as a DPSP.

questions.question: What is the title of the comprehensive report submitted by the National Commission on Self-Employed Women and Women in the Informal Sector during the Seventh Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shramshakti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The title **"Shramshakti"** refers to the comprehensive report submitted by the National Commission on Self-Employed Women and Women in the Informal Sector.
 
• This report was presented during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990)** of India.
 
• The report highlighted the challenges faced by women working in the informal sector, emphasizing their contributions and socio-economic issues.
 
• The commission was headed by **Dr. Ela Bhatt**, a noted social activist and founder of SEWA (Self-Employed Women’s Association).
 
• The "Shramshakti" report laid the foundation for policy recommendations aimed at improving the working conditions and social security of women in the unorganized sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990):**

 
 
• Focused on improving productivity and generating employment opportunities.
 
• Prioritized social justice and upliftment of marginalized groups, including women in the informal sector.
 
 
 
• **Informal Sector:**
 
 
• Comprises workers who are not covered by formal employment contracts, including domestic workers, street vendors, and agricultural laborers.
 
• Women form a significant proportion of the informal workforce, often lacking social security and legal protections.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Ela Bhatt:**
 
 
• A renowned social activist and founder of SEWA (Self-Employed Women’s Association), an organization aimed at empowering women workers in the informal sector.
 
• Instrumental in bringing attention to the issues of self-employed women through her leadership in preparing the "Shramshakti" report.
 
 
 
• **Policy Impact:**
 
 
• The "Shramshakti" report influenced various government policies aimed at improving the livelihood and social security of women in informal employment.
 
• It also led to the recognition of the informal sector as a crucial component of India’s economy.

questions.question: By which of the following names are the prayers written in Rigveda known?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sukta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The prayers and hymns in the Rigveda are known as **Suktas**, which means "well-said" or "beautifully constructed."
 
• Each Sukta is composed of several **Richas** (verses) that praise various deities, including Agni, Indra, Varuna, and others.
 
• The Rigveda contains **1,028 Suktas**, which are further divided into 10 Mandalas (books or chapters).
 
• These Suktas form one of the oldest known collections of religious texts and reflect early Vedic culture and spirituality.
 
• The Rigveda is written in **Vedic Sanskrit**, an ancient Indo-Aryan language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda:**

 
 
• It is the oldest of the four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• The text is estimated to have been composed between **1500 BCE and 1200 BCE**.
 
• The Rigveda primarily consists of hymns dedicated to natural forces and gods like Agni (fire), Indra (thunder), and Varuna (water).
 
 
 
• **Richa:**
 
 
• A Richa is a **verse or mantra** in Vedic literature.
 
• Each Sukta in the Rigveda is made up of multiple Richas.
 
• Richas are composed in a poetic meter and are used in Vedic rituals and ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Mandala Structure:**
 
 
• The Rigveda is divided into 10 Mandalas (books).
 
• Each Mandala is further divided into Suktas, which are collections of hymns.
 
• The **10th Mandala** includes the famous Purusha Sukta, which describes the cosmic creation.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Deities:**
 
 
• The Rigveda mentions numerous deities, including **Indra (king of gods), Agni (fire), and Varuna (cosmic order).**
 
• These deities represent natural forces and cosmic principles.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the term 'Public Debt'?

options.text: The total amount paid by the government to its lenders
Total revenue generated by the government
Total investment made by the government
The total amount of money owed by citizens of a country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The total amount paid by the government to its lenders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public debt refers to the **total amount borrowed by the government** from external or internal sources to finance its expenditures and obligations.
 
• It includes loans taken by the government from **financial institutions, foreign governments, and private entities.**
 
• The government pays interest on this borrowed amount, making public debt a financial liability for the country.
 
• Public debt is broadly categorized into **internal debt** (borrowed from domestic lenders) and **external debt** (borrowed from foreign lenders).
 
• It is a critical tool for managing economic growth, funding developmental projects, and addressing fiscal deficits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Internal Debt**

 
 
• This refers to loans borrowed by the government from domestic sources like banks, financial institutions, and the public through bonds and securities.
 
• Internal debt is usually raised in the local currency and does not directly affect the foreign exchange reserves.
 
 
 
• **External Debt**
 
 
• External debt is borrowed from foreign governments, international organizations like the World Bank or IMF, or foreign private entities.
 
• It is denominated in foreign currencies, which makes it sensitive to exchange rate fluctuations.
 
 
 
• **Gross Public Debt vs Net Public Debt**
 
 
• Gross public debt includes all government borrowing, while net public debt accounts for the debt after subtracting government financial assets.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Public Debt**
 
 
• While public debt can fund infrastructure and development, excessive borrowing may lead to fiscal stress and inflationary pressures.
 
• Sustainable debt management is crucial for maintaining economic stability.

questions.question: K Chandrasekhar Rao, who faced a major failure in the Telangana elections in 2023, belongs to which of the following political parties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Rashtra Samiti (BRS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **K Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR)** is the founder and leader of the Bharat Rashtra Samiti (BRS), a regional political party in India, formerly known as Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS).
 
• The party was renamed from Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) to Bharat Rashtra Samiti (BRS) in **December 2022** as part of KCR's efforts to expand its influence beyond Telangana.
 
• BRS, under KCR's leadership, played a significant role in the movement for the formation of the state of Telangana, which was officially created on **June 2, 2014**.
 
• KCR served as the first Chief Minister of Telangana after the state's formation and has been a prominent political figure in the region.
 
• The party's primary agenda includes promoting the welfare and development of Telangana while also aiming to expand its political presence nationwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana State Formation:**

 
 
• Telangana was formed as the 29th state of India on **June 2, 2014**, after bifurcation from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The demand for a separate Telangana state was based on cultural, economic, and historical differences with Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Rashtra Samiti (BRS):**
 
 
• The BRS is focused on regional development, addressing farmer issues, and providing welfare schemes for the people of Telangana.
 
• It has also initiated several flagship programs like the **Rythu Bandhu Scheme** and **Mission Bhagiratha** for rural development.
 
 
 
• **K Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR):**
 
 
• KCR played a pivotal role in the Telangana statehood movement and is known for his strong political strategy and governance style.
 
• He has been elected multiple times to the Telangana Legislative Assembly and Parliament of India.
 
 
 
• **Renaming to BRS:**
 
 
• The decision to rename TRS to BRS was taken to reflect the party's ambitions to expand its influence beyond Telangana and address national issues.
 
• The party's new focus includes a pan-India political vision under KCR's leadership.

questions.question: As per Employment Exchange Statistic 2023, what was the percentage of women jobseekers for Live Register in India in the year 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.356**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Employment Exchange Statistics 2023, the percentage of women jobseekers in the Live Register in India for the year 2022 was **35.6% (0.356)**.
 
• The Live Register refers to a dataset maintained by employment exchanges containing the number of jobseekers actively seeking employment.
 
• Women constituted a significant portion of jobseekers, reflecting the growing participation of women in the labor market.
 
• Despite the increase in women jobseekers, challenges like wage disparity, limited access to opportunities, and skill gaps persist in the Indian labor market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Live Register:**

 
 
• A statistical measure maintained by employment exchanges to track the number of individuals actively seeking jobs.
 
• It provides insights into labor market trends, including gender-based jobseeking patterns.
 
 
 
• **Employment Exchange Statistics:**
 
 
• An annual report published by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.
 
• It provides detailed data on employment trends, jobseeker demographics, and the performance of employment exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• The percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• In India, LFPR for women remains lower compared to men, highlighting the need for targeted policies to enhance women's workforce participation.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Initiatives:**
 
 
• Government schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) aim to bridge skill gaps and improve employability.
 
• Such initiatives play a key role in empowering women jobseekers to compete in diverse sectors.
 
 
 
• **Gender Equality in Employment:**
 
 
• Promoting gender equality in the workforce is critical for achieving sustainable economic growth.
 
• Policymakers emphasize equal pay, safe workplaces, and access to professional opportunities to address gender disparities.

questions.question: ‘Cheiraoba’ festival is the New Year festival celebrated in the state of ___________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cheiraoba** is the traditional New Year festival celebrated in the state of **Manipur**, India.
 
• It is observed in the month of **April**, marking the beginning of the new year according to the traditional Manipuri lunar calendar.
 
• The festival involves **ritualistic cleaning** of houses and offering food to deities, symbolizing the renewal of life and prosperity.
 
• People prepare special dishes and offer them at hilltops, as a way to seek blessings for a better year ahead.
 
• Cheiraoba signifies unity and cultural pride among the Manipuri people, blending religious and social practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipur’s Culture:**

 
 
• Manipur is known for its rich cultural heritage, including classical dance forms like **Ras Leela**.
 
• The state is home to several indigenous festivals, such as **Ningol Chakouba** and **Yaoshang**.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Manipur:**
 
 
• Manipur is located in Northeast India and is bordered by Nagaland, Assam, Mizoram, and Myanmar.
 
• The state is famous for its scenic landscapes, such as **Loktak Lake**, the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Lunar Calendar:**
 
 
• The Manipuri lunar calendar governs traditional festivals and rituals observed in the state.
 
• It emphasizes alignment with natural cycles and the phases of the moon.
 
 
 
• **Hilltop Rituals:**
 
 
• Offering food at hilltops is a vital part of Cheiraoba, symbolizing the connection between humans and nature.
 
• It is believed to bring blessings, prosperity, and harmony for the year ahead.

questions.question: Sangeet Natak Akademi, the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country, was set up in which year for the preservation and promotion of various forms of Indian music, dance and drama?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1953**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in the year **1953** by the Government of India.
 
• It is India's apex cultural institution dedicated to the preservation and promotion of **performing arts**, including music, dance, and drama.
 
• The Akademi functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• Its primary objectives include recognizing and honoring outstanding practitioners in the field of performing arts and providing financial assistance for the preservation of traditional art forms.
 
• The institution plays a pivotal role in showcasing India's rich cultural heritage through programs, festivals, and awards such as the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards**

 
 
• The awards are considered among the highest national recognition given to performing artists, teachers, and scholars of performing arts.
 
• It honors contributions in fields such as **music, dance, theater, puppetry, and other traditional art forms**.
 
• The awards were instituted in **1952** and are given annually.
 
 
 
• **National Institutes under Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• The Akademi supports several national institutions such as **Kathak Kendra** in New Delhi and **Ravindra Rang Manch**.
 
• These institutions focus on training, research, and promotion of specific art forms.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Traditional Arts**
 
 
• The Akademi provides grants and organizes workshops to ensure the survival of endangered art forms.
 
• It emphasizes the documentation and archiving of rare performances and techniques for future generations.
 
 
 
• **National Cultural Institutions**
 
 
• Alongside Sangeet Natak Akademi, India has other apex institutions such as Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts) and Sahitya Akademi (literature).
 
• These institutions collectively contribute to preserving India's diverse cultural heritage.

questions.question: Who became the highest wicket-taker in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 ODI tournament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohammed Shami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohammed Shami** became the highest wicket-taker in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 ODI tournament.
 
• Shami displayed exceptional bowling performance, taking a total of **23 wickets** during the tournament.
 
• His best performance came against New Zealand, where he recorded impressive figures of **7 wickets for 57 runs**.
 
• Shami's ability to deliver consistent breakthroughs in crucial matches played a key role in India's success in the tournament.
 
• He achieved this feat despite playing fewer matches compared to some other bowlers, showcasing his efficiency and skill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup:**

 
 
• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup is the premier ODI cricket tournament organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• It is held every four years, bringing together the best cricketing nations to compete for the coveted trophy.
 
• The 2023 edition was hosted by India, featuring 10 teams competing in a round-robin format followed by knockout stages.
 
 
 
• **Bowling Terminology:**
 
 
• **Wicket-taking ability:** Refers to a bowler's skill in dismissing batsmen and breaking partnerships.
 
• **Economy rate:** Indicates the average runs conceded per over, showcasing a bowler's control.
 
• **Strike rate:** Measures the average number of balls bowled per wicket taken, highlighting efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Mohammed Shami's Career Highlights:**
 
 
• Shami is one of India's premier fast bowlers, known for his ability to swing the ball both ways.
 
• He debuted for India in ODIs in January 2013 and has been an integral part of the team since then.
 
• Shami holds multiple records, including being the fastest Indian bowler to take 100 ODI wickets.
 
 
 
• **India's Performance in ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023:**
 
 
• India was one of the favorites in the tournament, finishing at the top of the group stage.
 
• Key players like Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and Jasprit Bumrah contributed significantly to the team's success.
 
• The team's bowling attack, led by Mohammed Shami, was instrumental in securing crucial victories.

questions.question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which union territory has the least percentage of population who are multidimensionally poor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, Puducherry has the **least percentage of population who are multidimensionally poor** among all Union Territories.
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures poverty based on multiple indicators, including education, health, and living standards, rather than just income.
 
• Puducherry's effective implementation of social welfare schemes and better access to healthcare and education have contributed to its low poverty levels.
 
• Data in the report highlights that Puducherry excels in most indicators of the MPI, including access to clean drinking water, sanitation, and electricity.
 
• The National MPI 2023 was developed by NITI Aayog in collaboration with Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is a measure that captures poverty using multiple factors, including education, health, and living standards.
 
• It is based on internationally recognized indicators and is used to assess poverty beyond income levels.
 
• The MPI considers factors like malnutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, access to clean water, electricity, and housing quality.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Reduction in Puducherry:**
 
 
• Puducherry has implemented various schemes, including free healthcare, subsidized housing, and education programs, to reduce poverty.
 
• The UT's small geographic area and relatively high urbanization rates also contribute to better management and delivery of public services.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog's Role:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog is the policy think tank of the Indian government, responsible for creating strategies to achieve sustainable development.
 
• It collaborates with international organizations like UNDP and OPHI to develop measures like the MPI.
 
• NITI Aayog’s focus on data-driven policymaking helps improve social welfare initiatives across India.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories and MPI:**
 
 
• Union Territories like Puducherry and Chandigarh typically perform better on MPI indicators due to concentrated governance and smaller populations.
 
• The MPI helps policymakers identify specific areas needing improvement to reduce poverty more effectively.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, who is considered as a real executive of a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Minister is considered the **real executive head of a state** in India, as per the Constitution of India.
 
• While the Governor is the constitutional head of a state, the Chief Minister exercises **real power and authority**.
 
• The Chief Minister is the leader of the ruling party in the state legislature and plays a pivotal role in **policy formulation and implementation**.
 
• He or she is appointed by the Governor, but the appointment is based on the majority support in the legislative assembly.
 
• The Chief Minister heads the state council of ministers, which is responsible for **advising the Governor** and carrying out administrative duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head of a state, similar to the role of the President at the national level.
 
• He or she acts on the advice of the Chief Minister and the council of ministers, except in specific discretionary powers.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and serves a term of five years.
 
 
 
• **State Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• It is headed by the Chief Minister and comprises ministers responsible for various portfolios such as health, education, and finance.
 
• The council collectively advises the Governor and is responsible for **day-to-day administration of the state**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Minister:**
 
 
• He or she is the chief spokesperson of the government in the state legislature.
 
• The Chief Minister coordinates the work of various ministries and ensures the implementation of policies and laws.
 
• He or she also represents the state in interactions with the central government.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature:**
 
 
• The state legislature consists of the legislative assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and in some states, the legislative council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
• The Chief Minister is usually a member of the legislative assembly and needs to maintain majority support to remain in office.

questions.question: AAI 50th All India Inter-Institutional Table Tennis Championships 2023 was organised by ___________.

Madhya Pradesh state table tennis association

questions.question: A body is dropped from a height of 20 metres with zero initial momentum; calculate its mass if it hits the ground with momentum 40 kg. m/s. (Assume the acceleration due to gravity 'g' = 10 m/s2)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 kg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The momentum (p) of an object is given by the formula: **p = mv**, where 'm' is the mass and 'v' is the velocity.
 
• In this problem, the final momentum of the body is **40 kg·m/s**, and we need to calculate its mass 'm'.
 
• Using the equation of motion, the velocity (v) of the body just before hitting the ground can be calculated as:

 **v = √(2gh)**, where 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity (10 m/s²) and 'h' is the height (20 m). Thus, v = √(2 × 10 × 20) = √400 = 20 m/s.
 
• Substituting the values of momentum (p = 40 kg·m/s) and velocity (v = 20 m/s) into the momentum formula (p = mv):

 **40 = m × 20** → m = 40 / 20 = **2 kg**.
 
• Thus, the mass of the body is **2 kg**, which corresponds to **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Momentum:**

 
 
• Momentum is a vector quantity defined as the product of mass and velocity of an object: p = mv.
 
• It has both magnitude and direction, and its SI unit is **kg·m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• Free fall refers to the motion of a body under the sole influence of gravity, with negligible air resistance.
 
• In free fall, the acceleration of the body is equal to the acceleration due to gravity (g), typically 9.8 m/s² (approximated as 10 m/s² in calculations).
 
 
 
• **Kinematic Equation for Velocity:**
 
 
• The final velocity (v) of a body in free fall is calculated using the formula: v = √(2gh).
 
• Here, 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity, and 'h' is the height from which the body is dropped.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Momentum:**
 
 
• The law of conservation of momentum states that in the absence of external forces, the total momentum of a system remains constant.
 
• This principle is fundamental in solving problems involving collisions and other interactions.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Which movement, led by Swami Dayananda Saraswati, advocated for a return to the teachings of the Vedas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Arya Samaj was founded by **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** in 1875 in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The movement aimed at promoting the **purification and revival of Vedic principles** and practices.
 
• Swami Dayananda advocated for the slogan "**Back to the Vedas**" (Vedo Ki Or Lauto) to revive ancient Indian culture and spirituality.
 
• The Arya Samaj opposed idol worship, caste-based discrimination, and superstitions, emphasizing the **monotheistic teachings of the Vedas**.
 
• It played a significant role in India’s social and cultural reform movements, including the promotion of **women’s education and widow remarriage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Dayananda Saraswati:**

 
 
• He was a reformer and philosopher who sought to restore the Vedas as the ultimate source of knowledge and truth.
 
• He authored the book "**Satyarth Prakash**" (The Light of Truth), which became the doctrinal guide for the Arya Samaj.
 
• Swami Dayananda opposed rituals, priestly dominance, and practices like child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Belief in the **infallibility of the Vedas** as the highest authority.
 
• Promotion of **universal brotherhood** and social equality.
 
• Advocacy for **education for all**, including women, and the establishment of educational institutions like the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools and colleges.
 
 
 
• **Social Impact:**
 
 
• The Arya Samaj played a key role in the movement against untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
• It encouraged progressive reforms such as **inter-caste marriages** and widow remarriage.
 
• It also opposed foreign rule and contributed to India’s freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Related Movements:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, also worked for reform but emphasized monotheism and modern education.
 
• The Prarthana Samaj promoted social reform but was more moderate in its approach compared to the Arya Samaj.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of the substance that forms the tooth enamel in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium hydroxyapatite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Calcium hydroxyapatite (Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2)** is the primary mineral that forms the hard, protective outer layer of human teeth known as enamel.
 
• Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, and its durability is due to the crystalline structure of calcium hydroxyapatite.
 
• This mineral provides strength and resilience to teeth, enabling them to withstand the forces of chewing and grinding.
 
• Calcium hydroxyapatite also plays a role in maintaining the natural whiteness and smooth surface of enamel, which is critical for oral health.
 
• The presence of fluoride in dental products helps to convert hydroxyapatite into fluorapatite, which is more resistant to acid attacks from bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tooth Enamel:**

 
 
• Tooth enamel is made up of 96% minerals, primarily calcium hydroxyapatite, with the remainder being water and organic matter.
 
• It is non-living tissue, which means it cannot regenerate or repair itself once damaged.
 
• Enamel erosion can occur due to exposure to acids from foods, drinks, or bacterial activity, leading to tooth sensitivity and cavities.
 
 
 
• **Hydroxyapatite in Bones:**
 
 
• Calcium hydroxyapatite is also a major component of bones, providing them with strength and structure.
 
• In bones, hydroxyapatite is embedded in a matrix of collagen, making them both strong and flexible.
 
 
 
• **Role of Fluoride:**
 
 
• Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel by forming fluorapatite, which is more resistant to decay.
 
• Fluoride is commonly added to toothpaste and drinking water to promote dental health.
 
 
 
• **Dental Health Practices:**
 
 
• Maintaining good oral hygiene, such as regular brushing and flossing, helps prevent enamel erosion and decay.
 
• Avoiding excessive consumption of acidic foods and drinks can protect enamel from damage.

questions.question: Which of the following can help in water conservation?

options.text: Halving the supply of drinking water
Killing animals to reduce their population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rainwater Harvesting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rainwater harvesting** involves collecting and storing rainwater from rooftops, surfaces, or other catchment areas to use for irrigation, household use, and other purposes.
 
• This method reduces dependency on groundwater, which is depleting at an alarming rate due to over-extraction.
 
• It helps in **recharging aquifers** and improving the groundwater table, particularly in regions experiencing water scarcity.
 
• Rainwater harvesting is a sustainable and cost-effective water conservation method, widely promoted in urban and rural areas.
 
• Implementation of rainwater harvesting systems in residential, commercial, and industrial buildings can significantly **reduce water wastage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Groundwater Depletion:**

 
 
• Groundwater is a vital source of freshwater, but it is being depleted rapidly due to over-extraction and lack of recharge mechanisms.
 
• Rainwater harvesting can help mitigate this issue by replenishing aquifers.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Water Conservation Practices:**
 
 
• Many regions in India have traditional water conservation practices, such as stepwells and tanks, which emphasize the importance of rainwater collection.
 
• Reviving these practices can complement modern rainwater harvesting techniques.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• Rainwater harvesting reduces surface runoff, minimizing soil erosion and waterlogging in urban areas.
 
• It also reduces dependency on municipal water supplies, lowering energy consumption for water pumping.
 
 
 
• **Policy Support:**
 
 
• Many state governments in India have made rainwater harvesting mandatory for new buildings to tackle water scarcity.
 
• Awareness campaigns and subsidies for installation are being provided to encourage adoption.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Census Commissioner to estimate the population of the persons belonging to ST communities in the state under the Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Bill, 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Central Government** has the authority to appoint a Census Commissioner for special population estimates, including Scheduled Tribes (ST).
 
• Such appointments are typically made under the provisions of relevant bills or legislations, such as the **Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Bill, 2024**.
 
• The Census Commissioner plays a crucial role in collecting and analyzing demographic data to ensure equitable representation for ST communities in legislative assembly constituencies.
 
• Population estimates of Scheduled Tribes are critical for implementing affirmative measures and ensuring compliance with constitutional provisions regarding representation.
 
• The Central Government oversees nationwide census operations, ensuring uniformity and accuracy in data collection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census in India**

 
 
• The Census in India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948.
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the **Ministry of Home Affairs** oversees the census operations.
 
• It is the most comprehensive source of demographic, social, and economic data in India.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**
 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are recognized under Article 342 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are communities that are socially, economically, and educationally disadvantaged.
 
• Reservation and affirmative action policies aim to uplift ST communities in areas such as education, employment, and political representation.
 
 
 
• **Representation in Assembly Constituencies**
 
 
• Article 330 and 332 of the Constitution provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• Population data collected through census exercises is used to determine the proportionate representation of STs in legislative bodies.
 
 
 
• **Key Legislative Processes**
 
 
• Legislations like the **Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies Bill** aim to align representation with demographic changes.
 
• These bills are passed by Parliament and implemented through relevant government departments.
